analysis.investment_thesis: Cohance (formerly Suven Pharma) is undergoing a radical transformation — name change, massive balance sheet expansion (assets nearly tripled to INR 5,568 Cr in FY25), and surging debt (borrowings from INR 65 Cr to INR 451 Cr) — all while core revenues and profits have been declining since FY22. You are paying 94.7x EV/EBITDA for a business with an 8.89% operating margin and contracting earnings.
key_strengths: High gross margin of 71.5% suggests underlying product quality and potential in oligonucleotide/ADC building blocks if the new business mix delivers
Promoter holding of 57.5% with meaningful DII ownership (21.6%) suggests institutional confidence in the transformation thesis
Historical OCF generation (5/5 positive years) demonstrates the legacy business generates real cash
key_risks: Operating margin of only 8.89% is shockingly low relative to the 71.5% gross margin — massive opex burden or revenue recognition issue deserves scrutiny
Net profit has declined every year from FY22 peak (INR 454 Cr) to FY25 (INR 265 Cr) — 42% cumulative earnings erosion while the stock remains expensive
EV/EBITDA of 94.7x is a screaming danger signal; even on forward estimates this looks extremely stretched
red_flags: Total assets nearly tripled in one year (INR 2,254 Cr → INR 5,568 Cr in FY25) with no corresponding revenue uplift — large acquisition without demonstrated integration or return
ROCE of 14.9% and ROE of 12.7% are below the 15% threshold for a business this complex — the capital allocation is destroying value
EV/EBITDA of 94.69x — this is not a valuation, it is a speculation premium on a turnaround that has not yet materialized
analysis.detailed_analysis: Invert, always invert. What would make this a terrible investment? A complex corporate transformation (name change, major acquisition) executed while core earnings are declining, at a valuation that assumes the transformation succeeds perfectly, managed by a company that cannot explain the gap between 71.5% gross margins and 8.89% operating margins. That is precisely what Cohance presents today. The jump from INR 2,254 Cr to INR 5,568 Cr in assets in a single year — with borrowings rising 7x — is a classic 'frequent acquisitions without clear integration success' red flag from the checklist. The legacy Suven Pharma CDMO business had genuine merit, but this transformed entity is now unanalyzable in its current state. The forward P/E of 35.9x still prices in a full recovery — a very large bet on execution. Until two years of post-acquisition financial data clarifies what has actually been bought and what returns it generates, this falls squarely in the 'too hard' pile.
